content.text: targeting the anagen hair follicles (scalp MC)
that develop over a period of weeks (painless & not pruritic)
: short hairs broken off a few mm from the scalp w/ tapering near the proximal hair shaft (exclamation point appearance) at the margins of the patches
-in some cases, hair loss may be diffuse
-hair regrowth may occur (fine white hair regrowth)
no erythema, inflammation, or scarring seen
: pitting ~30%, nail fissuring, trachyonychia (roughening of the nail plate)
: definitive dx – peribulbar lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrates surrounding the follicles
; may be observed in mild cases
Genetically predetermined progressive loss of the terminal hairs on the scalp in a characteristic distribution (pattern)
MC type of hair loss in men & women
; gradual in onset & usually occurs after puberty
; activation of the androgen receptor shortens the anagen (growth phase) in the normal hair growth cycle
•pathologic specimens show decreased anagen to telogen ratio
: begins as bitemporal thinning of the frontal scalp then involves the vertex
: thinning of the hair between the frontal & vertex of the scalp w/o affecting the frontal hairline
: widens blood vessels, allowing more blood, oxygen, & nutrients to promote the anagen (growth) phase
: androgen inhibitor (inhibits conversions of testosterone to DHT)
: ↓ libido, sexual or ejaculatory dysfunction, ↑ risk of high-grade prostate cancer,
•candida albicans (more likely to affect fingernails) & non-dermatophyte molds
: ↑ age, tinea pedis (including close contacts), psoriasis, occlusive shoes, immunodeficiency
•KOH wet mount prep: only 60% sensitive; rapid
Management initiated if KOH/PAS + while waiting for cultures
Infection of the lateral & proximal nail folds <6wks
: MC occurs after penetrating skin trauma (dishwashing, biting nails, cuticle damage during manicures, ingrown nails)
Painful, red, swollen area around the proximal or lateral nail folds at the cuticle
